newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAEL, PLO FAR APART DESPITE SECURITY TALKS.
newsitem.headline: ISRAEL, PLO FAR APART DESPITE SECURITY TALKS.

text.p: Israel and the Palestinians remained far apart on key issues in a peacemaking crisis even as their security men and a U.S. representative met in the West Bank enclave of Ramallah.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat rejected Israeli allegations that his planned "national unity" talks with militant Palestinian groups set for this week was an "appeasement of terrorism."
"No doubt we are against terrorist activities...but this is a Palestinian interest and we are insisting on carrying on dialogue with all Palestinian groups," Arafat told reporters in Gaza.
"We are as Palestinians completely committed to the peace process and at the same time we are facing collective punishment from the Israeli government."
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's communications chief David Bar-Illan had said earlier: "We don't believe that this kind of appeasement of terrorism works."

Israel, reacting to a double suicide bombing which killed 16 people including the attackers in a Jerusalem market last month, sealed off Palestinian areas and froze millions of dollars of financial transfers owed to the Palestinian Authority.
The bombing complicated U.S. efforts to break a deadlock in Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations, which stalled after Israel began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Netanyahu accused the Palestinian Authority of not fighting anti-Israeli guerrillas on its territory, while Arafat said Netanyahu was using the bombing to destroy the peace process.
Security men from the two sides and a U.S. representative met in Palestinian-ruled Ramallah as part of a framework set by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross who spent four days in the region last week.

Israeli security sources said the Palestinians gave them results of checks made on explosives found in early July at a West Bank apartment suspected of being a bomb laboratory of the anti-Israeli Hamas movement.

Ross was also preparing the ground for a visit by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright planned for September. She has demanded improved security cooperation before she makes her maiden trip to the Middle East.
Israel says Arafat must arrest anit-Israeli militants and crush the infrastructure of Islamist groups before it will lift the sanctions.
Washington has repeatedly condemned Israel's measures as counterproductive and unhelpful, while the Palestinians said they would match the sanctions with a partial boycott on Israeli goods.

The director general of the Palestinian Commerce Ministry, Nasr al-Sarraj, told Reuters that a number of goods produced in Israel were barred from Gaza including soft drinks, chips, biscuits, canned food, electronic products and cigarettes.
